slides.title: A position depends on layers
bullets: Settlement chain: Ethereum
Yield source (issuer): sUSDe, by Ethena
Pendle market: the PT/SY pool
Lending market: Morpho Blue, LLTV 91.5 %
Oracle: decides when liquidation happens
slides.notes: Found from the data (discover.py), not by hand: the issuer is the Pendle market's underlying, looked up in registry.json. Each layer gets a yearly probability p and a severity distribution.

slides.title: Exploit prior: from DefiLlama's hacks
slides.text:
p = clip( r_tier × m_category × f_age ,  0.5 %,  15 % )

r_tier: hacks per protocol per year, same size band, last 5 years
m_category: the category's hack rate ÷ all categories, kept in 0.5–2
f_age: 2 if listed < 1 year, 1 if 1–3 years, 0.7 beyond
slides.notes: priors.py exploit_p_year; registry.json frequency: years 5, floor 0.005, cap 0.15, tiers 10M / 100M USD, category clip [0.5, 2], age factors 2 / 1 / 0.7. Sizing by protocol size matters: by category alone, Morpho Blue got 15 %/yr, because small lending forks are hacked often.

slides.title: The terms, for the demo
table: lending is hacked more than average
kept at the floor of the clip
24 oracle exploits / 179 protocols / 5 y; ×2 if unverified
slides.notes: The oracle counts only misconfigured, stale or predictable-oracle exploits: spot manipulation of a thin token does not apply to a PT oracle. The demo oracle (MetaOracleDeviationTimelock) is verified on Etherscan, so no doubling.

slides.title: Market events: from the registry
bullets: A depeg is not an exploit: not in the hack record
registry.json sets p, severity and recovery, with a basis
sUSDe: 12 %/yr, average depeg 8 %, 75 % recovered
Basis: USDe near 0.65 on one CEX on 2025-10-10
Unknown issuer: 15 %/yr default, 60 % recovered
Severity: a Beta(a, b) draw, mean a / (a + b)
slides.notes: registry.json issuers.<address>.depeg and unknown_issuer. Every number carries its basis, shown in the report under Assumptions and their basis.

slides.title: From probabilities to losses
bullets: 20,000 simulated months (simulate.py)
Each layer fails with its 30-day probability
A failure draws its severity from its Beta
propagate.py turns shocks into the position's loss
True value vs oracle value: only the oracle liquidates
Only dependency: an issuer exploit brings a depeg
slides.notes: Same 10 % shock, very different losses: an sUSDe depeg seen by a market-tracking oracle liquidates (whole equity lost); with a fundamental oracle only the unrecovered part is lost (80,651 USD). Layers are otherwise independent: a known limit.

slides.title: What the simulation gives (demo)
slides.notes: VaR 95 % is 0: incidents happen in only ~2 % of months, so the tail is read at 99 %. Attribution: depeg 3,760, Morpho 1,066, oracle 747, Ethena 511, Pendle 353, Ethereum 16 USD of the expected loss.

slides.title: The verdict uses them
bullets: EXIT if expected loss > carry + exit cost
REDUCE if carry < expected loss, or CVaR 99 % > half the equity, or the liquidation distance < the stress drop
STAY otherwise
Exit not worth it: 78,946 USD to leave
slides.notes: decide.py verdict. The de-lever suggestion: sell 1.29M USD (33 %) to bring the liquidation distance to the stress drop; expected loss falls to 4,308 USD.

slides.title: Breakeven p*: no prior needed
slides.text:
p* = cost of leaving now ÷ loss saved by leaving first

Cost: the yield given up on what can leave, over the horizon
Saving: loss if staying − loss if leaving first
Per year: 1 − (1 − p*)^(365 / horizon)
Leave only if you believe the incident is more likely than p*
slides.notes: vault_incident.breakeven (D142–D143). p* ≥ 1: stay even if the incident is certain. Belem vault, mGLOeuro −30 %: leaving forgoes 2,229 EURCV of yield over 30 days, more than leaving first saves (383), so stay. f(x) vault, fxSAVE −30 %: p* 7.9 % over 30 days. A book acts first on the vault with the lowest p* (D144).

slides.title: Outside view: Nexus cover prices
right: Says what the cover pays on
slides.notes: nexus.implied (D146). Example: f(x) cover implies 1.2–13.7 %/yr for an exploit at the shock's severity. Protocol cover pays on an exploit, not on an issuer's NAV markdown or a borrower's default: the line says so.

slides.title: Limits
bullets: Base rates, not an audit of each protocol
Layers independent, except issuer exploit → depeg
Market-event priors are judgements, with a basis
A 5-year hack window: DeFi changes fast
Carry assumes today's rates over the horizon
slides.notes: docs/analysis/GAP.md discusses a shorter window (2 years) with a limited weight, and other signals (audits, reputation). docs/analysis/EXTERNAL_SOURCE.md §7 proposes a weighted blend of the internal priors with Credora, Nexus and Pharos.
